findings.title: Per-resource denial cache means every distinct denied resource triggers a DB permission requery
findings.body: When cached permissions don't allow the request, Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which always queries the DB because the cache lookup was removed from getUserPermissions. The denial cache is keyed by (user, action, name, parent), so it only suppresses repeats of the identical resource. A user who checks many different resources they cannot access, such as filtering a large list item by item, causes one permission-store query per distinct resource within the TTL. The singleflight key is per user and action, so it only collapses concurrent calls, not sequential ones. This can put a lot of load on the DB for exactly the denied-heavy workloads the cache is meant to protect.

findings.title: Denial cache can keep denying a user right after permissions are granted or a resource is created
findings.body: A denial is cached for 30s under (ns, user, action, name, folder), and nothing invalidates it. This includes name-less checks such as folders:create, where name and parent are empty. If a check for a resource runs before the user's permission exists (an existence probe before creation, or a permission granted moments later), the user is denied for up to 30s even after the DB is correct. That partly defeats the PR goal that creators can immediately access what they just created.

findings.title: Requery on cache miss refreshes permissions but not the folder tree
findings.body: On a cached-permission denial the code re-fetches permissions from the DB, but checkPermission then calls buildFolderTree, which uses the folder cache with a 30s TTL. A user who creates a new folder, or a dashboard in a newly created folder, can still be denied inherited access until the folder cache expires. This is because the new folder is not in the cached tree, so the requery does not fully fix the new-folder case.

findings.title: Deny-cache test does not prove the permission cache is bypassed; denial write path is untested
findings.body: The comment says the permCache entry 'allows access to prove this is not checked', but the value is set to false (`"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`). A map entry with false already means not allowed, so the test would pass even if the denial cache were ignored. Nothing tests that a denied Check actually writes the denial entry, that the entry is keyed correctly, or that an allowed check does not write one.

findings.title: getUserPermissions test left with dead cacheHit branches after the cache-hit case was removed
findings.body: The 'from cache' test case was deleted, so cacheHit is always false and the cacheHit branches (the s.permCache.Set and the `store.calls == 1` assertion) are dead code. The remaining case named 'should return error if store fails' expects no error. Together these make the test misleading, and the change that moved the cache lookup out of getUserPermissions has no direct test.
